hints: Notice the four values span from $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $300\,000\,000\text{ m s}^{-1}$ - think in orders of magnitude for sound in air.
Recall everyday evidence: thunder arrives seconds after lightning from kilometres away, giving speed of hundreds of metres per second.
Compare with the very large value $3 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ which belongs to light, not to a mechanical wave in air.
walkthrough: Identify the quantity: speed of a sound wave travelling through air at normal temperature, in $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
Recall the order of magnitude: sound travels about 1 km in about 3 s, so $v \approx 1000/3 \approx 330\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Compare each option: $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$ is 10 times too small, $30\,000\text{ m s}^{-1}$ is 100 times too large, and $300\,000\,000\text{ m s}^{-1}$ is the speed of light.
The value $300\text{ m s}^{-1}$ matches the expected hundreds of metres per second. This is option B

options.A: Too slow for sound - $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$ is about car speed, while sound crosses about 1 km in 3 s.
options.B: Sound in air is about $340\text{ m s}^{-1}$, so $300\text{ m s}^{-1}$ is the correct order of magnitude.
options.C: Far too fast - $30\,000\text{ m s}^{-1}$ is even faster than sound in most solids.
options.D: This is the order of the speed of light in vacuum, $3 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}$, not sound.
